findings.title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty
findings.body: In EventManager.create the code does const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [] and then reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is null, undefined or [] (which this PR explicitly allows and other call sites pass as []), mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and property access throws TypeError, aborting booking creation. It must use mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration.

findings.title: updateEvent calendar fallback can never work
findings.body: The new code is: const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId. In the else-branch externalCalendarId is falsy, so searching for cal.externalId === externalCalendarId can never match and selectedCalendar is always undefined. The previous fallback to event.destinationCalendar.externalId was lost, so updates without a stored externalCalendarId call the Google API with undefined calendarId and fail.

findings.title: deleteEvent calendar fallback can never work
findings.body: The new code is: const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId. When externalCalendarId is falsy the find predicate compares against that same falsy value and never matches, so calendarId is always undefined and deletion silently falls back to primary instead of the host destination calendar. The old fallback to event.destinationCalendar.externalId was lost.

findings.title: updateEvent called with undefined credential
findings.body: In updateAllCalendarEvents the code looks up credential by reference.credentialId in memory and then in the DB. If neither yields a credential, credential stays undefined but the code still does result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, ...)). CalendarManager.updateEvent then calls getCalendar(undefined), which throws/rejects and turns the whole reschedule/update into failures. The loop must skip or return a failure result when no credential was found.

findings.title: Patch after insert drops primary fallback
findings.body: createEvent inserts with calendarId: selectedCalendar || primary but the follow-up patch that adds the hangoutLink uses calendarId: selectedCalendar with no fallback. When no destinationCalendar matches the credentialId, selectedCalendar is undefined and the patch is sent with an undefined calendarId and fails, leaving the event description without the Meet link.
